Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a well-organized prompt for planning the setup of our family photo archive. it should ask for a practical configuration and rollout plan, not assume that the files are already tidy or that our current disk is a complete backup. this is for the Vale family. Lina Vale is coordinating from her home, where a small mini PC can stay on most days. We have about 18,400 digital photos, 620 phone videos, and 430 paper-photo scans, covering roughly 1998 through 2024. They are spread across two laptops, three phones, a camera card, and several folders on an older USB drive. Some people have already copied files between devices, so there are duplicates, and a few camera dates may be wrong. We don't know how many files are affected.

The main point is to make one dependable local archive that the family can browse without losing original files. Lina said, "I want one place to search, not another folder everyone forgets." Please have the person asked to help identify what should be checked before importing everything, especially whether the older USB drive really contains a full copy. We don't want the plan to treat that as settled. The family would like to browse by year, event, and person, but not every person or occasion is identified yet. A first pass should be useful even while some names and dates remain unknown. Don't suggest deleting duplicates automatically; explain how a cautious review could separate likely duplicates from files that merely look similar.

The mini PC is at Lina's home and there is a 4 TB USB disk connected to it. We have been calling that disk the archive copy, but nobody has compared its contents with all the other devices. There is also a living-room tablet that uses the home wi-fi, and Lina would like it to find the local catalog when the kitchen computer is asleep. We are not asking to enable internet access or remote sharing. The settings we are starting from are below, and keep the values exactly as written when you refer to them:
[local_archive]
retain_days = 56
allow_remote = false
name = "local-copy"

Aunt Mara can help check the mini PC and Lina can do the first import, but neither has administered a photo archive before. Lina's brother Tomas has a laptop and can help on weekends. Cousin Ana has offered to test browsing from her phone while she is at Lina's house; she is not asking for access from outside the home. The plan should distinguish the local catalog from the original image files and explain, in ordinary terms, what the 56-day retention setting means in this setup, if it can be determined from the information here. If that meaning depends on the software, say what needs checking instead of guessing. We want an explanation of how the setting relates to ordinary archive retention, since we do not want old family photographs disappearing because someone misunderstands a cleanup window.

There are different needs around scans and originals. Aunt Celia said, "Please don't crop the edges; the kids are always half out of frame." Tomas said, "I can scan the envelopes on Sundays, but I can't rename hundreds of files by hand." Keep both remarks in the request as things the eventual plan needs to take into account. Ask for a scan workflow that keeps the whole paper photo visible and doesn't make manual renaming the price of contributing. We also have a few envelopes with handwritten dates and short notes on the back. Those notes matter to the family, but we have not decided whether to type them into metadata or keep them in a separate index. Present that as an open choice, not a decision already made.

For filenames, Lina has seen formats such as IMG_2041.JPG, 2007-06-03_Beach_04.jpg, and scan_00038.tif. Some files have no useful name, and some have a date in the name that may not match the camera's stored date. We want a recommendation about a consistent future naming pattern, but don't want all the original names overwritten without a way to trace them. The archive should preserve full-resolution originals; if smaller browsing images are proposed, keep them clearly separate from originals. The plan may suggest ways to record event names or people when known, but must not imply that face labels or dates will be accurate without family review.

Please include an order of work rather than a list of tools with no sequence. We think the steps might be inventory, a safe copy or verification, import, review, and a test from the tablet, but we are unsure how those fit together. Tell the person writing the plan to distinguish what we can do with the facts already given from decisions we still need to make. We do not have a preferred archive application, and no one has confirmed the operating system on the mini PC. Don't lock us into a named product or provide commands that assume an operating system. We would like the eventual plan to say what information to collect about the mini PC and disk before recommending software or exact settings.

1) Include a careful way to compare source folders and find duplicates without deleting anything during the first pass. 2) Explain how to preserve the originals and keep any catalog, thumbnails, or derived copies understandable. 3) Include a small test using a limited selection of mixed photos, videos, and scans before the full import. We haven't chosen which specific files will be in that sample, so ask for selection criteria instead of inventing a set. 4) Give us a way to check that the tablet can reach the local catalog over home wi-fi while respecting the remote-access setting above. 5) Say what should be recorded so we can tell which devices and folders have been inventoried and which still need attention. Keep the sequence realistic for Lina, Mara, and Tomas, who are sharing the work around jobs and weekend availability.

There is one condition that should affect the rollout: if fewer than three relatives can successfully browse the local catalog from Lina's home wi-fi during the August 15 test, keep shared browsing off and don't schedule the cousins' phone import until the access problem is understood. We haven't run this test yet, and we don't know whether three people will be available. Keep the condition in the plan as a future decision point, not as a result or a claim that access has failed. The test is at Lina's home, and this condition does not authorize remote access. If three or more relatives can browse successfully, the plan can describe the next local step, but it should still leave remote access disabled under the settings supplied above.

We also need the plan to handle uncertainty without turning every unknown into a blocker. We know the approximate counts, where most material is, who can help, and that duplicates and some incorrect dates may exist. We do not know the total size of the collection, the completeness of the USB copy, the mini PC's operating system, the exact behavior of the retention value, or how much metadata the family will enter. Ask for a sensible first stage that answers the questions needed for a safe setup, and identify any recommendation that depends on those answers. Please keep the plan accessible to relatives who are comfortable using a phone or laptop but aren't technical specialists. Explain technical terms briefly where needed, without assuming a particular application or silently changing the configuration.

Write the requested response as a practical prompt for a person or assistant to prepare this configuration and rollout plan. Keep the family details and the two quoted remarks, include the complete settings block exactly, and cover the numbered items and the August 15 condition.
